description:
MEDIUM AND MATERIAL. Every token is the same thing: a loose cluster of flat, translucent, hard-edged polygons alpha-stacked on a near-black slightly warm charcoal ground. The vocabulary is narrow and consistent - rotated squares and rectangles at a range of scales, a smaller number of circles/discs, and occasional tiny diamonds. There are no strokes, no outlines, no gradients, no texture, no line work and no type. All form comes from flat fills overlapping at partial opacity, so the drawing is entirely made of accumulation: where two slate squares cross you get a lighter slate, where amber crosses slate you get a muddy olive-brown, where amber sits alone on the ground you get a dark tobacco brown. It reads as torn/cut translucent paper or stacked gel squares - a collage study, or a pile of tilted cards seen from above.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. Nothing representational. The nearest read is 'a scattered stack of tilted panels'. The one recurring form with real character is a notched, castellated polygon with stepped shoulders - clearest in seed 9369 and in the 512 single, where a slate notched slab sits on a big amber square - and it is the only mark in the system that looks drawn rather than assembled. Elsewhere the shapes are plain quadrilaterals.

PALETTE. Effectively two hues plus ground: a cool desaturated slate blue-grey and a warm amber/ochre. The ground is near-black. Ratio is heavily slate-dominant in most seeds with amber used as the single accent; only 9369, 10622 and (in stress) 9548 let amber take real area. 9906 is almost pure grey with no amber worth naming.

COMPOSITION. Every one of the twelve is a centred cluster floating in the middle of a square frame with a wide empty dark margin on all four sides. The frame is not used - nothing is cropped by it, nothing is anchored to it, nothing acknowledges an edge. The only seed that approaches the edge is 9369, whose big amber square nearly fills the tile. Focal hierarchy is inconsistent by seed rather than by design: 9369, 10622 and 10801 have a genuine dominant mass and read as figure-on-ground; 9011, 9727, 10085, 10264, 9548 are mid-density piles with a soft centre of gravity but nothing that commands; 9190, 10443 and 10980 are even scatters of small debris with no dominant element at all - confetti with a hole in the middle.

THE TWELVE, INDIVIDUALLY. 9011 leaning stack of ~8 similar-sized slate squares, one small amber lozenge and a pale disc at centre. 9190 loose scatter of a dozen small dark squares around a pale disc and one small amber square. 9369 the strongest - big rotated amber square nearly filling the tile with the slate notched slab across it. 9548 dense muddy pile of ~15 slate squares with an amber band through the middle-right. 9727 mid cluster with an amber wedge escaping at the left. 9906 the outlier - dominated by two large pale grey discs, almost no amber. 10085 compact cluster, amber square lower-left is the brightest thing. 10264 big loose pile of large slate squares with amber and a pale disc at centre. 10443 near-empty - tiny debris in the middle of a mostly black frame. 10622 big amber rectangle under and between large slate squares, second-clearest figure-ground. 10801 monolithic slate mass with amber leaking at the right edge. 10980 sparse debris, small amber knot at centre.

WHAT THEY SHARE AND HOW THEY DIFFER. They unmistakably share one system: same ground, same two hues, same alpha-stacking logic, same rotated-square vocabulary, same centred-cluster placement. What varies is essentially THREE dials - how many elements, how big they are, and how much amber is allowed. That is real variation of density and mass, but it is variation of quantity rather than of structure: no seed invents a different arrangement, a different composition strategy, a different relationship to the frame. The gap between 10443 (near-empty) and 9369 (near-full) is wide; the gap between 9011, 9727, 10085 and 10264 is small enough that they read as four shuffles of one deck.

MARKET STATES. The three rows are clearly different and the difference is legible, and it is consistent in direction across all four seeds shown. NEUTRAL is the most compact and settled - elements packed, amber contained, low tilt. STRESS disperses and heats: the cluster spreads, discrete circles and small diamonds detach and drift as satellites (9011 stress gains a disc at top-left and small diamonds lower-left; 9548 stress gains discs off to the right), rotation increases, and amber becomes both more saturated and much larger in area (9369 stress rotates its amber square and adds a second amber slab at the bottom; 9548 stress promotes amber to a big block at the top). RECOVERY does not return to neutral - it cools past it. The amber recedes and greys down, elements settle back into a flatter, more overlapped stack, and the whole thing loses contrast (9011 recovery is nearly monochrome grey with the amber almost extinguished; 9548 recovery is greyer and lower-contrast than its own neutral). 9369 recovery is the exception where recovery is the CLEANEST of its three - a big upright amber square with the notched slate form centred on it. So the arc reads: tight -> scattered and hot -> settled and cooled.

TOKEN IDENTITY ACROSS STATES. Each seed stays itself. Scale class, element count class, colour balance and rough placement all persist: 9190 is a scatter in all three states, 9369 is 'big amber square plus notched slate slab' in all three, 9011 is a leaning mid stack in all three. 9548 moves the most - its amber migrates from mid-right in neutral to a dominant block at the top in stress - but the pile character survives.

AT 120PX. The system survives as a system but loses most of its interior. The dense seeds (9548, 10264, 9727) collapse into a grey smudge with an orange smear through it - the individual squares stop being countable and the alpha-stacking becomes mush rather than structure. The sparse seeds go the other way: 10443 at 120 is a few grey specks in a black square and barely reads as an artwork at all, and 10980 is close behind. The seeds that hold are the ones with one big mass and strong hue contrast - 9369, 10622, 10801, 9906. Comparing 120 against 256 confirms this is loss rather than my eye: at 256 you can count the squares in 9548, at 120 you cannot. Twelve tokens at 120 still look like more than three or four distinct things, but the middle-density group blurs toward each other. The state rows remain distinguishable at 120 - the stress row's detached satellites and hotter amber and the recovery row's greying are both visible.

ARTIFACTS. No hard clipping at the viewBox that I can see; nothing is cut in half by the frame. The visible flaws are compositional rather than technical: heavy alpha stacking produces muddy indeterminate mid-tones in the dense seeds where six or more shapes cross, so the overlaps read as accident rather than as construction; the amber-over-black brown (visible bottom-left of 9369 neutral, left of 9727) is a dead dirty colour that neither of the two chosen hues asked for; and the small detached squares in 9190 and 10443 read as leftovers rather than as placed elements.
